The Death of the PC Has Not Been Greatly Exaggerated
Wired knows how to spin a title. It's not a death just a shift in the market. Funny though how many sites still whiff on mobile.

I feel as if those old laptop docks may actually have a comeback in the future. I'd love to be able to use my dual monitors and keyboard for gaming, and then take my tablet out of the dock and hop in bed and watch some videos. Though the technology isn't there, I can maybe see it happening in the future.

My Phenom II X6 has been humming along for 5 years now @ 4ghz. Sure it sucks a lot of juice and keeps me warm in the winter but it still plays everything I throw at it.

I'm sure the same can be said of overclocked C2Q's, and early I5/I7's. Software pushes PC sales. There is very little an overclocked 5 year old processor, 8 GB ram, and a decent 3 year old video card can't handle.

The PC industry is slowing down because people don't need to upgrade.

I've been hearing this crap for 20 years, adding niche devices simply spreads out the userbase, it doesn't eliminate it. No matter how advanced a mobile device becomes, even if it reaches parity with the best PCs(which isn't even possible), none of that will matter. Until there is a way to interface with a mobile device at the same level or better than a PC, such as a keyboard/mouse or any HID, PCs will always exist.
PC's definitely have and will continue to have a great portion of the market. They are workhorses, strong and powerful, but rooted.
Same thing that has been said when consoles became powerful.
